products.name: AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper Edition Solar Cellular Trap Camera with Remote Trigger (Standard)
specs: Built-in 9 V relay on low-voltage leads, fired from the AnywhereCam app (9 V battery not included)
220 V / 3 A, IP65, 2-pin 15 mm nut connector
4G LTE; maker says it joins the strongest of Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, US Cellular and regional carriers
$18.67 a month per camera (1-10 cameras), unlimited data, no contract
Full-color HD (resolution not stated), 120° view, 355° rotation
Solar panel with battery; up to 14 days without direct sun (maker claim)
8 GB microSD included; cloud optional at $6.95 a month
About 2 weeks; built to order in Colorado
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty for the original buyer; a defective unit is replaced with the same model, shipped free.
products.returns: 30 days from delivery. Request a return first and AnywhereCam sends a label. Full refund only for unused items in as-new condition.
products.summary: A solar 4G camera with a built-in relay you fire from the phone app. Watch the trap live, then drop the gate once the whole sounder is inside. Camera and trigger are one device on one data plan, and it isn't tied to one gate maker.
products.fit: Owners of an existing corral or box trap whose gate has, or can take, an electric latch or solenoid release, who want the camera and the trigger in one solar unit.
caveats: No gate or latch included: you need an electric release that a 9 V relay can fire, and AnywhereCam publishes no wiring guide.
Remote use needs the AnywhereCam data plan, $18.67 a month per camera.
Built to order: allow about 2 weeks before it ships.
Video resolution and infrared wavelength are not stated, and we found no independent field review.
1-year warranty, shorter than the 3 years HogEye states.

products.name: AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Wireless Trapper Edition, Cellular Trap Camera with Wireless Gate Trigger (Standard)
specs: Camera, transmitter and receiver; the receiver's 9 V relay fires from the AnywhereCam app (9 V battery not included)
4G LTE; maker says it joins the strongest of Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, US Cellular and regional carriers
$18.67 a month per camera (1-10 cameras), unlimited data, no contract
Full-color HD (resolution not stated), 120° view, 355° rotation
Solar panel with battery; up to 7 days without direct sun (maker claim)
About 2 weeks; built to order in Colorado
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty for the original buyer; a defective unit is replaced with the same model, shipped free.
products.returns: 30 days from delivery. Request a return first and AnywhereCam sends a label. Full refund only for unused items in as-new condition.
products.summary: The same solar 4G trap camera, but the trigger goes over a wireless link to a receiver at the gate, so no wire has to run from the camera to the latch.
products.fit: Trappers who want the camera across the trap or up a post, away from the gate, with no cable through the pen.
caveats: The maker publishes neither the transmitter's range nor how the receiver is powered. Ask before you buy.
Costs $100 more than the wired Trapper Edition.
Battery is rated up to 7 days without sun, half the wired version's 14.

notes: QUERY: Google autocomplete suggests 'hog trap camera trigger', 'hog trap camera system', 'remote hog trap trigger/gate/door', 'cellular hog trap trigger/gate'. Current results are thin: maker pages (HogEye, JAGER PRO), forum threads, one gate roundup (bestdeerfeeders) and low-quality scraped pages. PAIN POINTS (count of sources/posters): cost of systems and data, 6 sources (bestdeerfeeders, talkbusiness $8,000+, WPLN about $3,000 per unit, Predator Masters 2 posters, Deer Hunter Forum $30/mo, farmstandapp); no signal at the trap, 6 (bestdeerfeeders, Deer Hunter Forum, farmstandapp, Texas A&M, talkbusiness, Tiger Droppings BoarBuster pole antenna); wiring the trigger to the gate, 3 (Predator Masters 2 posters, bestdeerfeeders retrofit note); lock-in or network shutdown, 2 (Predator Masters on JAGER PRO's proprietary trigger and a dropped 3G camera, Deer Hunter Forum on the AT&T 2G shutdown); spooking from IR glow and shutter noise, about 4 posters in one Trapperman thread plus Campark. SEGMENTS: (1) existing trap, wants camera plus trigger cheaply: AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper ($457 Standard vs JAGER PRO solar camera $618, data $18.67/mo unlimited vs $40/mo for 5 GB, generic relay vs JAGER-only gate, maker-claimed multi-carrier vs one carrier); (2) buying a full trap: JAGER PRO Corporal ($3,500 text camera / $3,800 live stream, 6 panels, verified on jagerpro.com 2026-11-10); (3) camera away from the gate: Wireless Trapper ($557); (4) DIY: any cell camera plus a GSM relay. PRICES VERIFIED 2026-11-10 on anywhere.cam: the storecheck product endpoint returned HTTP 429 on every retry (it succeeded once, for the Eagle 4G Pro: $245, compare-at $370). Trapper variant prices came from the store's own /search/suggest.json on anywhere.cam: Trapper Standard $457, Outpost $557, Refurbished Standard $409; Wireless Trapper Standard $557, Outpost $657, Refurbished $409; all available. NOTE: storecheck search reports $409 for both Trapper listings, but that is the refurbished variant. Records use the new Standard prices. The product URL may open on a different default variant. Data plan: the pricing page says $18.67/mo per camera for 1-10 cameras ($15.37 for 11+), but the FAQ still says plans 'start at $24.95'. I used the pricing page and store product ($18.67). Cloud is $6.95/mo. Warranty is 1 year; returns are 30 days with a free label. CODES: none. The site banner says 'Black Friday Sale! Save $125 on cameras' with no code, and the Trapper variants have no compare-at price, so it likely doesn't apply to them. No network codes were given. UNVERIFIED, kept off the page or labelled: Trapper video resolution and IR wavelength; Wireless Trapper range and receiver power; real multi-carrier roaming performance (maker claim, and the page says 'AnywhereCam says'); HogEye hardware and plan prices (dealer listings show $2,199 and $65/mo but couldn't be re-read, so the HogEye row shows 'not listed'); Hogg Boss $599 conversion unit (only on scraped mirrors, left out); BoarBuster price ($8,345 on a dealer page, not on the page). No independent reviews of AnywhereCam exist that I could find (no Reddit, Trustpilot or BBB hits). That is stated in the caveats. JAGER PRO's data price ($40/mo for up to 5 GB) is from its $599 non-solar Live Stream page; the $618 solar page doesn't list a data price.
